svg.title: Diary block updates and same-Diary resume links
svg.desc: A new task appends a working block. A related correction checkpoints and updates that same block. Completion or cancellation changes that block's status. Explicit pause preserves it as paused; resuming appends a linked working copy at the bottom. Completing the copy completes the paused source chain in the same Diary. Fast changes logging time; nod skips logging.

g.text: When to edit, when to append, and what stays linked
All blocks below belong to one Diary. Independent tasks and child Diaries have separate lifecycles.
A · ORDINARY WORK AND RELATED CORRECTIONS
New task request
Append a new bottom block.
Record prompt + ordered plan.
Block N · Working
Exact prompt, plan, progress, lessons.
One stable entry ID.
Complete or cancel
Update Block N's real final status.
No duplicate completion block.
Related correction or a new priority while work is active
Checkpoint first → append exact “+” prompt → revise the plan.
Continue the same Block N. Do not silently mark it paused or finished.
B · EXPLICIT PAUSE AND RESUME
Source Block N · Paused
User explicitly pauses the work.
Save the checkpoint and status.
Retain the original in place.
Resume
New bottom Block M · Working
Copy N's content; assign a new number, entry ID, and timestamp.
Place the exact resume prompt above the original request; revise the plan if needed.
resumes_entry_id → N's entry ID · resumes_block_number → N
Finish M → complete M and its linked paused source chain
The update is atomic within this Diary. N stays paused until the copy completes.
Cancel M → cancel M only; its source remains paused.
M is the next allocated number,
not necessarily N + 1.
C · TAGS CHANGE RECORDING, NOT THE MEANING OF COMPLETION
Terminal (fast) · work first, then log
Preserve new-task / correction / resume relationships.
If interrupted and unfinished, keep the work Working.
Terminal (nod) · no Diary operation
No block, correction, or later backfill for that prompt.
If both terminal tags are present, (nod) wins.
Labels are English explanations. Existing on-disk Korean lifecycle identifiers are preserved for compatibility.
